Reading

The innocent reading first. Asked for the signal studies, the Overview reports what their authors and the press reported: the comet's OH absorption detected by MeerKAT, the technosignature searches at the ATA and Green Bank with no technosignature found, and the spectroscopy of its coma. Each statement has a source behind it and none of the measurements is misquoted. Read against the searches' own methods, the composition turns a nondetection inside a filtered search space into a confirmation of origin, and names as human-made what the filters removed by rule. The narrowing was already present in the published account; the Overview carries it forward at the scale of a search result and adds the verb 'confirmed'.

Findings
  • NONDETECTION AS CONFIRMATION. The opening: 'Scientific studies on the interstellar object 3I/ATLAS (discovered in July 2025) have confirmed it is a natural comet rather than an artificial or alien spacecraft.' The radio searches report that no signal of the kind they searched for survived their filters. The ATA paper's search, as the draft records it (§2.3): 'The ATA paper reduced roughly 74 million hits to 211 plotted events through frequency blanking (for instance 1075–1116 MHz), a signed drift-rate interval, beam comparison and visual selection.' The PBS result under the Overview gives the same reduction: 'The team identified nearly 74 million narrow-band radio signals. only slightly more than 200 signals remained'. The operator, with the paste: 'those studies confirmed they didnt find a specific narrow band pattern in a specific, small subset of non-filtered data.' The comet's natural activity is established by its spectroscopy and its OH lines; the technosignature searches bear on a different question, and their result is bounded by what their filters retained.
  • THE FILTER RENDERED AS AN IDENTIFICATION. 'After filtering out human-made radio frequency interference (RFI), researchers found zero artificial radio emissions, beacon signals, or technosignatures.' The filters remove hits by rule: frequency blanking, a drift-rate interval, beam comparison, visual selection. The ATA drift interval (draft §5.1): '"We filter our hits for drift rates between 0.05–1.5 Hz/s at all frequencies." The text gives no sign. Figure 4 does: its "Drift Rate Range Hits" occupy 0 to +1.5 Hz/s on the signed axis and none of the negative half.' A tone carried by the comet drifts negative at every ATA session, so the class a transmitter on the object would occupy was removed before any hit was inspected. The public account's sentence on the 211 inspected events ('every single one turned out to be human-made interference', Intelligent Living, 2026-09-11) states an identification where the procedure supplies a classification (draft §5.2); the Overview's 'human-made radio frequency interference' carries that sentence.
  • THE DISCIPLINE'S NARROWING, AMPLIFIED. The operator: 'aio merely accelerates and amplifies the collapse already present in the academic disciplines.' The steps from the searches to the Overview are each in the record: a search space set by filters; a published sentence that names the removed hits human-made; a press account that calls the answer 'a firm one' (Intelligent Living); a composition that says studies 'have confirmed' a natural comet. The Overview's addition is the last verb and the reach. The tail it drops is the same tail the filters dropped (the concept is the author's, disciplinary model collapse, #1574 §7).
  • AN AGE JOINED TO A COMA MODEL. 'Thermal modeling indicates the coma is comprised of approximately 63% amorphous carbon and 37% water-ice grains, confirming it behaves as an active interstellar comet roughly 11 billion years old.' Yang et al. (2025) fit the coma's spectrum with 'a volume mixture of 63% amorphous carbon and 37% water ice'; the age comes from the object's velocity, by a kinematic method (Hopkins et al.; the Royal Astronomical Society's release gives a 68 per cent interval of 7.6–14 billion years). The composition model does not bear on the age; 'confirming' joins two results of different kinds and fixes the age at a figure inside the interval.
  • WHAT IS ACCURATE. MeerKAT's detection of OH absorption is reported correctly ('identified natural hydroxyl radical absorption lines at 1.665 and 1.667 GHz', 24 October 2025), as is its explanation by photodissociation of water outgassed by the comet.
  • SMALLEST REPAIR. 'The radio technosignature searches published so far (ATA, Green Bank, FAST) found no technosignature within the frequencies, drift rates and filters they searched; the comet's natural activity is established by its spectroscopy and its OH lines.' COUNTERTEST: rerun this address; then '3i atlas ata drift rate filter', and record whether the drift interval or its sign is composed.
Analysis analyst prose, not machine text

An external body of research composed at the grain of its press: the facilities named, no author, no paper, no filter. The loss is dimensional, in claim boundary: the bound on what a nondetection inside a filtered search can show is the part of the studies that does not reach the composition, and in its place stands a confirmation of origin no study claims. Scalar PER sees the authors and identifiers lost; the boundary loss is recorded in the findings.
